top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is an original, experimentally verified invention: the magic-wavelength lattice lets many neutral atoms be interrogated without a trapping-light shift, it has been reproduced at the 10^-18 level in independent laboratories, and it has already opened laboratory tests of gravitational redshift and fundamental physics. It is a new door for measurement, not a later refinement of the comb or ion-clock work already honoured. Katori's original magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's realisation to 10^-18 give a clean two-person allocation with a citation scope that matches the record of who did what first, so I prefer awarding it to no award.
